title.narrative: Emergency Shelter Kits Assistance Project to IDPs in Tigray Region, Central Zone, Axum, Adwa, and Abiy Adi Towns

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian situation in the Tigray region resulted from the conflict continued to be aggravated and complicated from time to time. The living situation and shelter conditions deteriorate as a result of harsh weather, rain, windstorms, and limited resources allocated for maintenance and other infrastructure. Currently, the region hosts 760,406 IDPs still living in a difficult situation, including in collective centers and schools. According to DTM SA R37, the Central Zone hosts 196,229 IDPs (25.7%), yet shelter capacity remains critically low, compounded by prolonged resource shortages, overcrowding, and fragile shelter structures. As of March 2025, only 3% of the Cluster’s target population (501,000 individuals) had been reached with shelter or NFI assistance.ltbrgtThe proposed project aims to support IDPs in need of critical ESNFI support in Central Zone, Adwa, Axum, and Aby Adi, which host 39,814, 37,266, and 36,154 IDPs, respectively. Considering the high needs and the limited resources, Nexus Ethiopia targets a total of 3500 IDPs HHs or 19250 IDPs to get Emergency Shelter Kits (including for PWD, people with chronic illness, and older persons). The planned response is in line with the standard guidelines of the ES/NFI Cluster. On top of the ES/NFI cluster recommendations, to determine the feasibility of response, Nexus Ethiopia will conduct a joint beneficiaries selection and targeting with the key stakeholders in the IDP camps in Axum, Adwa, and Abiy Adi towns. The ES in-kind support improves the shelter conditions. The project will get 5000 plastic sheets from IOM core pipeline as in-kind support, which will be distributed to 2500 HHs. The remaining plastic sheet needs will be procured from local market.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented over a period of six months. 15% of the total beneficiaries will be PWDs, older persons, and persons with chronic illnesses. The project mainstreams a conflict-sensitivity perspective and implements a do-no-harm approach to reduce tensions and potential conflicts in the community. Nexus Ethiopia will coordinate closely with the ES/NFI cluster at the National and regional levels, UN, INGOs, and other relevant clusters, such as the CCCM cluster or CCCM partner OSSHD, to ensure a coordinated response. Nexus Ethiopia adheres to the Core Humanitarian Standards (CHS) and to national and cluster standards during the provision of assistance, including providing priority to PWD, the elderly, and women-headed HHs. Nexus Ethiopia applies an age, gender, and diversity lens to all phases of the project cycle and will work closely with protection experts to maximize benefits and mitigate protection risks. Overall, the project contributes to the overarching ES/NFI cluster objectives and the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), priorities set for Tigray by the national and regional ES/NFI cluster, EHF allocation strategy, and Tigray region humanitarian response plan through saving the lives of IDPs in the project locations.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
